detail: _intact() iterates `results` once for the integrity guard; the precedence code then iterates it again. No test feeds it an iterator.

# results = run_rules(make_proposal(), make_context(controls=Controls(kill_switch=True), clock=make_clock(False)))
outcomes: ['REJECT', 'PASS', 'REJECT', 'PASS'] ...
tuple     -> (<Verdict.REJECT: 'REJECT'>, 'kill_switch')
generator -> (<Verdict.AUTO_EXECUTE: 'AUTO_EXECUTE'>, None)
iter()    -> (<Verdict.AUTO_EXECUTE: 'AUTO_EXECUTE'>, None)

title: A daily-loss trip before the open halts only until that same day's open, so a P&L recovery later that day reopens trading
detail: _halt_instant uses clock.next_open whenever it is after now. That follows SPEC §4.4 to the letter, but when the trip is judged while the market is closed before a session (for example `evaluate --latest` at 08:00 New York), next_open is 09:30 the same day. The halt expires at the open, and a proposal judged at 09:31 with recovered P&L is AUTO_EXECUTE, which is what the requirement says must not happen ("a P&L recovery later in the day does not reopen trading"). An intraday trip correctly halts to the next day's open. This is a spec-level decision for the lead.
repro:
cd /tmp/aegis-gov.AxHmnZ && PYTHONPATH=/Users/test1/aegis /Users/test1/aegis/.venv/bin/python p7_halt.py   (section h, temp store)
# 12:00 UTC: evaluate(p1, ctx(now=pre, daily_pnl=-2500, clock=make_clock(False, next_open=13:30 same day, next_close=20:00)), conn)
('REJECT', 'market_hours') halt: 2026-07-30 13:30:00+00:00
# new connection, 13:31 UTC the same day, daily_pnl=+50, market open:
09:31 the SAME day, P&L recovered: ('AUTO_EXECUTE', None, {})
suggested_fix: When the trip is judged with the market closed, halt through the coming session rather than to its open, e.g. halt_until = max(next_open, next_close) when `not clock.is_open` and both are known. This over-halts by one session for an after-hours trip; the precise rule needs the exchange date of next_open. Pin it with a pre-market trip followed by a same-day recovery, expecting REJECT by halted.

title: An OSI-padded option symbol ("SPY   260821C00640000") evades the no-trade list
detail: underlying_of (aegis/policy/models.py:42, LOCKED) returns the OCC root unstripped, so the padded 21-character form yields the underlying "SPY   ". The store models only strip the ends of a symbol, structure_problems finds nothing wrong, and no_trade_list compares "SPY   " with "SPY" and PASSes. With watchlist_only off, an option on a no-trade underlying becomes NEEDS_APPROVAL instead of REJECT, and the audit line reads "SPY    is not on the no-trade list". With watchlist_only on (the default) the padded root fails closed at watchlist_only; exposure() strips and is unaffected; max_open_positions counts it as a new underlying, which is the conservative direction. It is never AUTO_EXECUTE, since it is an option.

detail: All seven required forms fail the test, in aegis/cli/policy.py and in aegis/brain/cycle.py. Rule (b) matches the token `Executor` only, as the spec and D4 define it. The conventional way to hold an instance is a parameter, variable or attribute named `executor`, and that plus a call to the interface's own methods (submit_order / cancel_order) passes every static rule and the runtime backstop. title: A cap of zero (or slightly negative buying power) still passes a notional of up to 1e-9 dollars to AUTO_EXECUTE
detail: `exceeds` allows an absolute slack of 1e-9 whenever both figures are below 1. With auto_execute.max_notional = 0.0, buying_power = 0.0 or buying_power = -1e-10, a buy with a $2e-10 notional is "within" the cap and the verdict is AUTO_EXECUTE. The amount is economically nil; the point is that a zero limit does not mean "nothing". Same root as the closing-sale finding. Separately and by spec: a notional of 1000.000001 against max_notional 1000 also auto-executes (relative 1e-9); 1000.00001 does not.

title: The engine trusts an unvalidated RuleResult: a garbage halt_until makes decide() raise, a None detail is accepted as PASS
detail: _checked verifies type, name and outcome only. A rule that returns a RuleResult built with model_construct gets through: with halt_until="tomorrow" on daily_loss_limit, _halt_to_persist calls `_aware("tomorrow")` outside the fail-closed try block and decide() raises AttributeError, so there is an evaluation without a verdict. With detail=None on auto_tier the result is accepted as PASS and the verdict is AUTO_EXECUTE with a null detail in the audit trail. Only reachable through a broken or monkeypatched rule. Everything else tried (raise, None, str, tuple, dict, wrong name, wrong outcome type, nameless callable, 19/21/reordered/empty registry) fails closed.

title: evaluate --dry-run, limits and kill status rewrite the file header of a database that is not in WAL mode
detail: _open_unchanged uses store.connect, which runs `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` before query_only is set. On a normal WAL store the main file stays byte-identical (verified). On a database in DELETE journal mode (a VACUUM INTO copy or a restored backup) the three "write nothing" commands switch it to WAL. No table row changes. This is the Phase 3 `connect` convention, inherited.

cd /tmp/aegis-gov.AxHmnZ && PYTHONPATH=/Users/test1/aegis /Users/test1/aegis/.venv/bin/python p9_dryrun.py   (temp stores; sha256 of the db file before/after each command)
WAL db   | evaluate --dry-run   rc=0 sha same=True rows same=True ...
DELETE db| evaluate --dry-run   rc=0 sha same=False rows same=True journal_mode now=wal
DELETE db| limits               rc=0 sha same=False rows same=True journal_mode now=wal
DELETE db| kill status          rc=0 sha same=False rows same=True journal_mode now=wal
suggested_fix: For the commands that must write nothing, open read-only (`sqlite3.connect("file:<path>?mode=ro", uri=True)` with the same row factory and pragmas) instead of store.connect, or document that a non-WAL database is converted. Low priority.

title: AUTO_EXECUTE is reachable with part of the account unreadable (conforms to SPEC §4; for the lead's decision)
detail: The lens asked that no unknown context field yield AUTO_EXECUTE. Every field §4 says a rule needs does reject (see `checked`). Three cases still auto-execute, all as §4 is written: (1) an equity buy with cash or options_buying_power None/NaN/inf/negative, since no rule reads them for an equity; (2) any context whose `errors` is non-empty, since no rule reads it (e.g. "account state: the broker reported no usable cash"); (3) a genuine closing sale with equity and buying_power unknown, because rules 8 and 9 PASS a closing sale before looking at them.
